steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Put 2 tablespoons sugar in a small bowl; set aside.
Sift flour, ginger, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt together into a medium bowl.

Beat butter and 1 cup sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in egg; stir in molasses and water. Gradually stir flour-spice mixture into molasses mixture until well combined.
Shape dough into 24 walnut-sized balls with floured hands. Roll each ball in the reserved sugar to coat.
Place cookies 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets; flatten slightly with the bottom of a glass.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops crack and centers are soft, 8 to 10 minutes, switching racks halfway through.
Remove from the oven; let cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

review.reviewBody: One of the best cookies EVER. Made them for Xmas to bring to school. They sat untouched compared to all the extravagant other cookies, but I forced people to try them. The result: my friend held two cookies in each hand literally SHOVING them in his mouth because they all got eaten in five minutes; there was a mad rush to get them and needless to say I brought none back home. Only problem with the recipe I can see is that the dough is very sticky and hard to form in balls. My suggestion is to drop the dough directly into the sugar and then form the balls as the sugar coats the dough and allows you to roll it. Also, I used a tablespoon of orange juice instead of water to bring out the ginger flavor and it worked extremely well.

These cookies are delicious!! They are also easy to make but you need to let the mix sit for a good 40-50 minutes before rolling into cookie form, otherwise you'll just be playing with a big gooey mess. I wish I knew that before I got my hands in it.

these cookies are very tasty, granted, yes. however, i was terribly annoyed to find that i had big gingerbread balls because of the directive: lightly flatten cookie. you need to really flatten the cookie out to get a result like that in the photo. i would make them again, and will really squash em down.

Yes, these are good and turn out perfectly, but I don't think they're as extraordinary as other reviewers seem to. This is a basic gingersnap recipe, found in nearly every cookbook, so there's nothing unique about it. For best flavor use butter, and chill your dough till semi-firm, about an hour, to make handling easier and to prevent them from spreading too much. I made mine a little bigger using a small ice cream scoop so they all turned out the same size, and "underbaked" them a bit to ensure a soft cookie. An easy cookie to make--perfect for the novice baker!

Wonderful cookies! Before I made these, I read probably 1/2 the reviews and tips. I decided to make it with extra ginger.. simply divine! 
I saw in a few reviews that they added more flour, or they omitted the water (liquid) altogether.. I don't recommend this. You can add 1 Tbsp of liquid to any cookie recipe if you want it to be softer/chewier. This is the trick for any cookie recipe. 
Another tip, I took out the very first batch exactly at 10 mins, but they were falling apart as I was transferring it to the rack, so I carefully put them back on the baking sheet and waited for the batch that was in the oven to finish baking (14 mins is best for me) then I placed it back in the oven and it rose up again and after 5 mins it was perfect. 
For the extra sugar sprinkling, I dipped the bottom of the dough ball in sugar; placed it on the sheet, then I dipped my fingers in the sugar and flattened the tops halfway. I also found that you must cool completely before you put in a jar or they will fall apart and mush up. 
Thank you for this awesome recipe!

This is a 5-star cookie IF they followed the original recipe posted a few years ago (no idea why it was changed?): 2 Cups all purpose flour, 2 tsp baking soda, 1.5 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp salt 1/4 tsp ground all spice, 1/4 tsp ground cloves, 1/2 Cup vegetable shortening, 1/4 Cup unsalted butter, softened, 1/2 Cup packed brown sugar, 1/4 Cup molasses, 1 Large egg. Topping: 1/4 Cup plus 1 Tblsp of turbinado sugar (or use regular sugar). So glad I wrote it down, they should really state how the recipe has been changed over the years. So many of the 5 stars were for the original recipe. Rotate halfway through baking time (350, 9-11 min) and then feel free to cool on wire racks.

I substituted brown sugar in the mix ( almost out of white sugar) and refrigerated the dough for an hour before using an ice cream scoop to measure the cookie dough out evenly. Rolled in white sugar. Dough was easy to scoop out and not sticky at all . I like the idea from the reader who used OJ in place of water. I’ll try that next time! Fantastic, family favourite

I made it exactly as written...except, in addition to the ginger powder, I added about 1.5 inches of grated fresh ginger to the creamed sugar and butter. I also let the dough sit in the fridge for 30 minutes so that the flour got good and hydrated. Very good!

Made first time per recipe. Cookies tasted fine, but came out flat and greasy. Second time, I used just one stick butter in place of margarine. I used orange juice in place of water and added a tsp baking powder. I also chilled overnight and did not flatten cookies at all before baking. These turned out perfect.

Great recipe! A few mods I made because our family likes them ginger-y... 1. Increased cinnamon to a full tsp. 2. Added a couple of tablespoons of crystallized ginger (chopped) 3. Used brown sugar instead of white for the dough. 4. Did not add water 5. Did not squish. Added to the softness! Did not chill dough, but suspect it would have been easier to make into balls and roll in sugar if it had. Will do next time!

These are my favorite cookies. I use butter instead of margarine (because margarine is not food), and I add a heaping tablespoon of nutmeg as well as using a heaping measure of the other spices. I also use a duck egg when my ducks are laying instead of a chicken egg, and chill the dough for a couple of hours in the fridge before making the cookie balls and rolling them. You can also chill for ten minutes in the freezer if you're in a hurry. Chilling makes the c ookies plump up more as they bake. My partner also loves it when I add raisins, so I add those in after baking a couple of sheets worth since I don't personally like raisins.

Perfect fall cookies! I followed the recipe as written. However, I didn’t roll in hand or flatten at all. I simply scooped with cookie scoop into my hand dipped tops in sugar and placed on tray to bake. 10 minutes in my oven and they were perfectly cracked and baked.
Delicious
More cooking time needed, mine were severly undercooked and made me sick
will try again but i believe the recipe meant to include baking powder not baking soda.

Thin and greasy, clearly this recipes ratios are not right. In my picture (the second round)i did overbake a tad but i tried two rounds, adding more flour the second time. Tastes alright but go find literally any other recipe. Made an account just to warn people.

For those complaing about the cookies being too flat, after rolling in sugar, do NOT flatten them, but sprinkle the tops with a drop or 2 of water. This crackles the tops and the cookies stay soft for a week. If they last that long! It's the only way I make mine and they have always turned out perfectly.
I made them for a gathering and told the guests were my taste testers. Everyone loved them!
The dough didn’t come out right and cookies were flat

I was really looking forward to baking these cookies, but I ended up feeling stressed out, confused and disappointed. I LOVE soft, chewy cookies. Absolutely dislike hard crunchy cookies. I had two issues with the recipe. First, it gives an "estimated" baking time. I realize ovens vary and times are subjective, but the indicator that the "tops are cracked" is VERY misleading. I was expecting to see open cracks like those in ameretti cookies. I never saw them. The tops stayed smooth the entire time which led me to believe I was doing something wrong. PLEASE revise the recipe to replace "cracked" with a better description of what indicates "done" (especially given having to guess baking time). I was originally going for 8 minutes to make sure they stayed soft, but gave them an extra 2 minutes to see if cracks appears. They never did. The centers were still a little soft. I baked the second batch even longer for the cracked indicator to appear. It never did. They are hard round ginger disks. I had to throw them out. I will try them again (not tonight) now that I know this. I want to make sure anyone who looks this far into the recipe before trying them doesn't have the same experience I did.
